utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: Well, for example, Branko Sekulic was wounded, he couldn't walk. We had to drag him along. We hoisted him up onto that cart. That's an example. But the rest of us, we were not really particularly strong by that time.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well. Continue describing this trip. Where did you go from the elementary school in this village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: We were transferred on this cart from the elementary school to Konjevic Polje. There, we came to a room, whether it was some sort of headquarters, or something like that. We came into this room and were questioned; where we were from, who we were. Specifically, they asked me why I had returned from Serbia, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Thank you. I just want a bit more detail about this encounter that you're describing. Firstly, who were the men who questioned you? I want to know if they were in civilian clothes or in uniform, and I want to know if they were armed or not.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: Well, they were in uniforms. Some were and some were not, as far as I could tell. I think that there was somebody there in command, at least that's how it looked to me, because he put questions to us and wanted to get our personal details.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you see this person who was apparently in command, so you say, giving orders or issuing orders to other men around him? I'm not talking about the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: Well, I suppose that he was in command, because he interviewed us. Now, whether he issued orders to somebody or not, I don't remember, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you see any paraphernalia, equipment around the place other than camouflage -- and uniforms, and armaments, that might be associated with soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: Equipment? I don't know what you mean.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Okay. Did you see anything like radios, walkie-talkies, rocket-launchers, any sort of heavy machine-guns, helmets? That sort of equipment.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I can't say. I don't remember those things. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Thank you. And lastly, were your fellow prisoners, Branko and the rest of them, were they also questioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: They questioned everyone, naturally.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And was the only topic that you are asked about the reason that you had gone to Serbia, or did the person you thought was of -- as a commander, also cover other topics other than why you went to Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: Well, that's what he asked me, you know, why and where I was from, details about my origin, and why I had come back. This is what he asked me. I don't know what he asked other people. I don't remember, and I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Thank you. From there, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: From that place, we went to Srebrenica. We took the road to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you go through any small villages or towns?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: Yes, we passed through the town called Kravica. I don't know how far that place is from Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How were you travelling at this point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: We were travelling in a van, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And can you tell the Trial Chamber if you were accompanied by armed men; and secondly, whether -- if there were armed men, how they were dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: There were several people who were in uniform, some kind of a camouflage uniform, and they accompanied us, escorted us, in the van and then further on. There were three or four of them. I couldn't tell you exactly, but that's how it was as regards Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you've mentioned Kravica. Did you drive through Kravica itself or skirt around it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: I think that that was the road which took us through Kravica. I don't remember exactly, I don't remember the details, but I think they passed through Kravica. I couldn't describe the road to you, but I saw that place. It's a town that could be described as a bit larger village.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, did you see any people in Kravica; and if so, what were they doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: As we were passing, I saw that they were collecting barrels and loading them up, and also some other items. That's what I could see as we passed through. I didn't see other things.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you see any horses in Kravica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: Well, yes, that's -- they were mounting those things on a horse.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: On a horse or several horses, or can't you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't really tell how many. I had no time for that. I just saw that they were loading things up, and that they were rolling some barrels.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you tell the Trial Chamber if you have any impression of how these people, who were rolling barrels and putting things on horses, were dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: Well, that was quite at a distance from me, so I couldn't say how they were dressed. There were women there too, you know. Women, men. And they were quite away from me. I couldn't tell you whether they were in uniforms or not. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well. We'll move on. From there, did you go through Potocari, and eventually on to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, from there we got to a place outside of Kravica. I don't know the name of that place. We got out of the van there, and then continued on foot across the hill, towards Potocari.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Thank you. And from Potocari, did you go into Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: From Potocari, we were put on a truck and transferred to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And the same party of prisoners that you've mentioned, Branko and Dragan, and so on, the people you've mentioned as having set out on this journey, were all of them taken to -- including yourself, taken to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: Yes, yes, all of us together.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: At any point in your journey were you ever unaccompanied; that is, did the guards -- the men who were with you, and some partially dressed in camouflage uniforms and some armed, did they ever leave you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: No. We all travelled together, we were together. Some people would come and go, but those who were with us were with us. And on our way there, we would come across some people - I don't know whether they simply caught up with us or joined us - but they would come and go.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Were the people who came and went and who joined up with you from time to time dressed in camouflage uniforms, or partially dressed in camouflage uniforms, and armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: Some were in partial uniforms, some were not. Some had weapons, some didn't. That's what I could see then.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Had you ever been to Srebrenica before, before this occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you arrive at night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: They took us to the entry point into Srebrenica. There could have been a police station or something like that there. And this is where we got out. In that place, they beat us thoroughly.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Describe to the Trial Chamber how you were beaten. And I want to know in particular whether instruments were used.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: Several young men came in. They had some sticks on them. They came in and they started hitting us so that I don't remember what happened afterwards. Later on, when I came to, when I got up, I saw that there were some armoires there or some shelves, and that they had fallen down. The three or four of them - I don't know exactly how many there were - beat us very badly.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you lose consciousness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: Yes, naturally. Naturally. As they beat us, we naturally fainted.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You may or may not be able to recall this, but can you tell the Trial Chamber if any of the guards who had accompanied you were present either before or after or during this beating.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: You mean in Srebrenica, when we got there?

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: I'm talking about this beating when you arrived. When you first arrived, you've told us that you were beaten. Now, if you can't tell us, that's fine. But if you can remember, can you tell the Trial Chamber whether any of the guards who were with you on the truck on the way into Srebrenica were present either shortly before you were attacked or during the beating or immediately after?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: No, I don't remember that. I don't know whether they were there or not.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: We need to go into private session, if Your Honours please, as I want to -- as I want to show the witness a document that may identify him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Following this beating that you were described in your evidence, were you taken somewhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: From there, they took us to a building which is at the end of Srebrenica, near the hill. This is where the building was, and this is where they took us from the place where they had beaten us.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You say, "They took us." Do you refer to the whole party, including the men that you've mentioned and Andja?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: Yes, the people who had been arrested. This is the people I meant. I don't know the people escorting us, I don't know them.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And there, in this other building that you're talking about, were you locked up into a room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: No. We came all together into a room and found people there already, who were detained there.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Other prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: Yes, other prisoners.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: All right, okay. Now, you've told us that you spent some time in Srebrenica, and it's not in dispute that eventually you left after some time. Did you remain in that room for the duration of your stay in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: Yes, we spent all of the time in that room, at least for as long as I was there.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you ever leave the room, for example, to go to the lavatory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: The lavatory was there, inside, and that was the one we used. There was another room - I don't remember clearly - that they took me to, and they hit me there. I can't remember specifically how big the room was, but I know that it was in the same building.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Apart from being taken out to be attacked and assaulted, and so on, did you spend the vast, overwhelming majority of your time locked up in this room that you're now talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: The room was locked. There were people there who made sure that it was locked. They probably watched the prison and took care of everything.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You've mentioned that -- you've mentioned that --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Your Honours, I just want to finish this topic, and we can stop at a natural break, if that's okay.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You've mentioned that Andja was there, was taken to the building. Was she put into the same room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: No. She was taken to a different room, and I think there were some other women there who were being held there.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What makes you say that, that there were women, other women, apart from Andja?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C007
utterances.text: I said this because, during the time I spent there, there was a child who came to our prison to visit the grandfather, or at least that's what the child said. There was an old man in the prison who the child referred to as the grandfather. And the child also said his mother was being held there alongside with several other women.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, this is as good a time at which to stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perfect. I thank you, Mr. Di Fazio. Witness, we will resume tomorrow morning. Tomorrow morning we have the option of working in Trial Chamber I, I understand; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, I will have it confirmed in the morning. The important thing is that the technicians know precisely that that is available so that it's -- okay, so you can proceed with making all the preparations to have the various protective measures in place, implemented. I thank you. Also, tomorrow, you have been advised that we will need to finish early because of a personal matter that I have to attend to. Yes, you will be escorted out of the courtroom now. You will return tomorrow morning. There's only one thing I need to tell you, sir, namely, not to talk to anyone on the matters that you are testifying upon, not to have contact or accept to have contact with anyone, all right? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 3rd day of February, 2005, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.48 p.m.,
